transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I think what finally made me come in is that my neck, my shoulders, and my jaw are just tight almost all the time now. It feels like I'm constantly bracing for bad news, even when there's no reason to. Like, even when I'm just sitting at my desk, or trying to watch TV at night... I just can't seem to relax my muscles.
Besides the muscle tightness, have you noticed yourself worrying a lot, more days than not, about several different things—like work, health, or family—and finding it hard to control that worry?

Yeah, I have. It's honestly hard to stop it once it starts. My mind just keeps jumping around from one thing to the next. 

I'll be worrying about whether the contractors missed something in the house, and then it immediately shifts to work—like whether my lesson plans are slipping, or if the kids in the robotics club are falling behind. And then I just end up worrying that I'm disappointing my wife and my family by not keeping everything under control. It's just a constant loop of things I can't stop thinking about.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worrying and muscle tightness—has it been going on for six months or more?

Yeah, it has. I'd say it's been going on for about seven months now. It really started when a pipe burst at our place, and the remodeling just threw the whole house into chaos. The worrying and the tightness just haven't really stopped since then.
Have you been having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling like your sleep isn't restful?

No, not really. My sleep has actually been pretty normal. I mean, once I finally lay down and close my eyes, I usually fall asleep fine and stay asleep through the night. So, no, sleep hasn't really been an issue for me. It's mostly just during the day that I can't turn my brain off.
Have you been feeling more tired or easily fatigued lately, even without doing much physical activity?

Yeah, I have actually. It's... well, by the time the last bell rings at school, I just feel completely wrung out. And it's a kind of tired that a decent night's sleep or even a quiet Sunday doesn't really seem to fix. It's gotten to the point where even just sitting down to grade a short stack of quizzes feels like I'm pushing through mud. I just don't have the energy I usually do.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating lately, or times when your mind suddenly feels blank?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with that. My focus seems to be about the same as it always is, and I don't get those moments where my mind just goes blank. I can still get through my lesson plans and everything just fine, so concentration isn't really a problem for me.
Have you noticed yourself feeling more irritable or on edge than usual, even over small things?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, teaching teenagers requires a pretty long fuse anyway, but I haven't noticed myself snapping at anyone or getting unusually frustrated over little things. My patience seems to be about where it usually is, so irritability hasn't really been a problem.
Do you ever feel physically restless or 'keyed up'—like you can't sit still or need to keep moving—even when you're trying to relax?

Yeah, I do. I feel pretty wound up most of the day, honestly. It's like... well, like I'm just waiting for something else to go wrong. I actually catch myself pacing around the empty classroom a lot. And between periods, I'm constantly checking my phone to see if there are any new messages from the contractor. It's just really hard for me to just sit still and relax right now.
